metadata.title: Fix invoke_tool crash on duplicate tool names across teams
metadata.author: kevalmahajan

description:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR

Closes #2863

## 📌 Summary
Fixed a bug where invoke_tool crashed with MultipleResultsFound when multiple tools existed with the same name (even if they belonged to different teams or owners). The lookup logic now correctly handles duplicate names by filtering based on user visibility and prioritizing the most relevant tool.



## 🔁 Reproduction Steps
1. Register a mcp server with name `gitmcp` in one Team A
2. Register same mcp server with same name `gitmcp` but in different team named Team B
3. As a user in Team A or Team B, invoke any tool in gitmcp server:
Before: The system attempts to fetch weather solely by name, finds two records, and crashes with sqlalchemy.exc.MultipleResultsFound.
After: The system detects both tools, filters for the one accessible to the user (Team B's gitmcp tool), and successfully invokes it.

## 🐞 Root Cause
The invoke_tool method used a naive database query:

```python
tool = db.execute(select(DbTool).where(DbTool.name == name)).scalar_one_or_none()
```
This query enforced global uniqueness of tool names, which contradicted the system design that allows tools to be "shadowed" or duplicated across different scopes (Private, Team, Public). When a collision occurred, SQLAlchemy raised an exception because it found multiple rows when it expected at most one.

## 💡 Fix Description

Updated invoke_tool in `mcpgateway/services/tool_service.py` to handle potential name collisions:

1. Fetch All Matches: Changed the query to fetch `scalars().all()` instead of `scalar_one_or_none()`.

2. Optimized Fast Path: If only one tool is found (the common case), it is returned immediately, preserving existing performance constraints.

3. Context-Aware Resolution: If multiple tools are found, we resolve the ambiguity by:
Filtering: Excluding tools not visible to the user (e.g., Private tools of others, Team tools of non-member teams).
Prioritizing: Sorting accessible tools by scope precedence:

- Team Tool 
- Private/Personal Tool
- Public Tool 

4. Ambiguity Guard: If multiple tools exist at the same priority level (unlikely given constraints but possible), explicit error handling is now in place to return a clear error instead of a crash.

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Good catch on the `MultipleResultsFound` crash — this is a real bug when the same MCP server is registered across multiple teams.

Rebased onto main, squashed the 7 commits into 2 clean ones, and applied the following fixes:

**Security fix:** Replaced the hand-rolled visibility filtering with `_check_tool_access()` to ensure consistent access control. The original filtering was missing the `is_public_only_token` check, which meant a public-only token (`token_teams=[]`) could access private tools if the `owner_email` matched.

**Cache fix:** Added a `multiple_found` flag to skip caching when multiple tools share a name. Without this, the first user to invoke the tool would cache their resolved result, causing false "not found" errors for users who should resolve to a different tool.

**Other fixes:**
- Removed duplicate comment block
- Fixed priority comment to match code (`team > private > public`)
- Renamed misleading test (`test_lookup_prioritizes_private_over_team` → `test_lookup_prioritizes_team_over_private`)
- Added tests for cache-skip behavior and public-only token filtering

All 4446 service tests pass. New code has 100% line coverage.

commits.message:
fix: handle duplicate tool names across teams in invoke_tool

Change scalar_one_or_none() to scalars().all() to prevent
MultipleResultsFound crash when the same tool name exists in
multiple teams. Filter candidates through _check_tool_access
and prioritize by visibility (team > private > public).

Closes #2863

Signed-off-by: Keval Mahajan <mahajankeval23@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>

commits.message:
fix: reuse _check_tool_access for multi-tool filtering, skip cache on duplicates

- Replace hand-rolled visibility filtering with _check_tool_access
  to ensure consistent access control (is_public_only_token, admin
  bypass, team DB fallback)
- Skip cache when multiple tools share a name since resolution is
  user-dependent
- Fix duplicate comment block and misleading test names
- Add tests for cache-skip behavior and public-only token filtering

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
